div.p: talaimakaṉ piriviṉkaṇ vēṟupaṭṭa talaimakaḷatu vēṟupāṭukaṇ ṭāṟṟāḷāya tōḻikkut talaimakaḷ colliyatu.
What SHE said to the confidante who could not bear it when seeing the changes in HER who had undergone changes during the separation from HIM.

lg.l: Alas, oh friend, what of the rumours
in this village, for many days?
Even though my young beauty [and] good gracefulness will be lost,
like the Vēmpi of Mucuṇṭai with many spears
every day when singers petition with the sweet voice of the clear kiṇai drum,
with worn-away drumsticks that are tied [and] bound with leather straps of generous length,
putting before [them] bulls with eminent, swaying, graceful humps that are covered with sandal paste,
fixing gold to [their] horns [and] putting on [them] golden garlands,
heaping ample cooked food [for them] together with elephant bulls [and] tall chariots,
– he who traversed the glittering mountains vanishing in bamboo,
where herds of Uḻai deer run,
crying out when parting, each on another crossroad way,
after thinking [that] the dusty-mouthed west wind, that stirred up the field reeking of flesh
when the warriors with wreaths of peacock feathers,
resting in the lingering shade of the forest with many flowers,
fell a young cow [and] eat [its] meat,
[is] the gripping voice of the strong tiger with sickle stripes
that rose to hunt prey on the slope of the tall mountain.
